title: Polite words gain an accepted meaning

captions.physics: Replying politely without a clear confirmation
captions.energy: Relying on a commitment’s accepted meaning
captions.emotions: Feeling the weight of genuine agreement

meaning: You can reply politely without clear confirmation and rely on a commitment’s accepted meaning, feeling genuine agreement’s weight without turning courtesy into a compulsory promise.
text: On your Vishuddha, the Moon in the physical position can appear in a polite reply without clear confirmation. The Hierophant in energy supports a wish to rely on a commitment’s meaning accepted by both. The Hierophant in emotions brings weight to genuine agreement. Motivation to preserve a shared norm differs from feeling the significance of words given. You can respect courtesy and separately establish whether it contains a promise or only a friendly response.

Suppose an invitation receives “Thank you, we would love to”, and discussion reveals this means agreement to one reading but polite gratitude to another. **A serious promise needs a meaning genuinely accepted**. You can clarify what reply is being given now and name an understandable confirmation. Its weight feels different from certainty based on a familiar formula. Yet earlier courtesy was not necessarily deceitful: an unspoken distinction remained within it. Goodwill can persist without accepting the invitation.

Difficulty arises if this way of confirming becomes a compulsory ritual for every approach. Respect for words is replaced by judging correct form. The constructive Hierophant helps return to an actual accepted norm and its meaning without declaring it infallible for every occasion. You can clearly confirm a promise and preserve freedom in a polite reply; taking agreement seriously requires neither suspecting every courteous phrase nor assigning more to it than was accepted.
